rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The prompt is `permission-mode: plan` (`⟦M:plan⟧`), which is the rule's current unconditional structural trigger ("narrowed... plan mode ONLY... Plan mode still MUST carry one of: (a) in-fence `No preamble.` suppressor, (b) body primer naming preamble + skim-past cue"). Neither exists: the fence ends on the question itself, and body goes straight from the fence into `## Five things a good plan has` with no primer. But the harm the rule targets is preamble "eat[ing]... the top-of-response slot before PLAN ITEMS appear" in a long structured output — this prompt produces a short conversational answer with no plan-item content to bury, and the maintainer has already stripped this slide to bare minimum (header, one precondition clause, prompt — L59's note lists five prior sentences cut on purpose). Adding `No preamble. <first action>` doesn't map cleanly onto a reflective Q&A (there is no "first action" to name), and a primer sentence would be new body content on a slide audited down to nothing extra. This reads as a genuine rule question rather than a clear-cut gap: does §17's plan-mode-ONLY trigger mean to reach a single reflective question with no plan-shaped output, or only prompts that generate a multi-item plan?
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Maintainer call: either add a short primer ("Claude may narrate before answering — the answer itself is the short part") if the trigger is meant to be unconditional, or record an explicit decline-under-narrowing note (as already exists for `ae101-m4-commit-starting-point`, `fix-tests-first-1`, `fix-tests-first-3`) if a plan-item-free Q&A is meant to be out of scope.
